caches.registry.default.hitMeaning: a lookup answered from the cache
caches.registry.default.notCountedWhy: the lookup is in a file this repository does not edit
caches.store.acme.nonces.title: ACME nonces
caches.store.acme.nonces.description: The Replay-Nonce values already presented to the ACME server (RFC 8555 section 6.5), so each is accepted once.
caches.store.acme.nonces.bound: Enforced: acme.maxSpentNonces spent nonces per realm. Expired ones are cleared at the bound; a history still full REFUSES the next spend (answered badNonce) rather than forget a live one.
caches.store.acme.nonces.lifetime: Until the nonce expires; expired ones are cleared when the limit is reached.
caches.store.acme.nonces.hitMeaning: a nonce already spent, so the request was refused
caches.store.applications.listing.title: Application registry listing
caches.store.applications.listing.descri: Every application entry in a realm, parsed, with a lookup per client_id, audience, AppliesTo and permission — so a page or a token request does not parse the whole registry per question.
caches.store.applications.listing.bound: Structural: one listing per realm, the size of ou=applications (itself capped by applications.max).
caches.store.applications.listing.lifeti: Until anything under the realm's ou=applications changes; the next read then parses it again.
caches.store.applications.load.title: Application entries read by identifier
caches.store.applications.load.descripti: One application's entry and its parsed record, by identifier, so the checks a sign-in makes do not read and parse the entry per question.
caches.store.applications.load.bound: Enforced: MAX_LOAD_MEMO (256) identifiers per realm; past it the kept answers are dropped.
caches.store.applications.load.lifetime: Until anything under the realm's ou=applications changes; the next read then asks the directory again.
caches.store.applications.ssf-allowed-ev: Which application owns a Shared Signals stream and which events it may receive, per principal, so a session event does not walk every registered application.
Enforced: 4096 answers per realm, the oldest dropped and looked up again when next needed.
Until anything under the realm's ou=applications changes; the next lookup then empties that realm's answers.
caches.store.attribute-sources.lookups.d: The row an attribute source returned for one person's key, held briefly so a burst of sign-ins is one query (#94).
caches.store.attribute-sources.lookups.b: Enforced: 2000 rows per process, the oldest dropped.
caches.store.attribute-sources.lookups.h: a sign-in answered from a lookup made seconds before
caches.store.attribute-sources.lookups.s: {{seconds}} s after the lookup; a change to the source drops its rows.
caches.store.authn.session-window.title: Sign-on session window
caches.store.authn.session-window.descri: The sign-on sessions one process holds when authn.sessionWindow is on (#350). A miss is read from the sealed row. Eviction forgets the memory copy after the upsert has committed and does not end the session.
caches.store.certificates.parsed-facts.d: The subject, issuer and notAfter a certificate list shows, and whether a certificate carries a post-quantum key, parsed once per certificate for /admin/pki and GET /admin-api/certificates. Keyed by the certificate's own SHA-256.
caches.store.certificates.parsed-facts.b: Enforced: 4,096 certificates, the oldest dropped and parsed again when next shown.
caches.store.certificates.parsed-facts.l: No expiry: keyed by the certificate's content, whose facts never change. The oldest goes first when full.
caches.store.credentials.totp-verdicts.d: Whether each sealed authenticator (TOTP) secret this process has been asked about opens under its key-encryption key (#352), so the users list and the second-factor roster can report an enrolment as readable or not without unsealing it on every request. Keyed by the sealed text; the value is yes or no, never the secret.
caches.store.credentials.totp-verdicts.b: Enforced: 20000 verdicts; full, the oldest is dropped and that secret is opened again when next asked about.
caches.store.credentials.totp-verdicts.l: Until the key-encryption keys change, or it is dropped to make room. A new enrolment is a new sealed text and is asked afresh.
caches.store.credentials.totp-verdicts.h: a sealed secret whose verdict was already known, so it was not opened
caches.store.debugger.static-files.title: Embedded debugger static files
caches.store.debugger.static-files.descr: The embedded debugger's client files with this service's address substituted in, kept per file version and address so the debugger listener does not rewrite a file on every request.
caches.store.debugger.static-files.bound: Enforced: 400 files, the oldest dropped and read again when next served.
caches.store.debugger.static-files.lifet: Until the file changes on disk (a new modification time is a new entry); the oldest goes first when full.
caches.store.devices.challenges.title: Device enrolment challenges
caches.store.devices.challenges.descript: The challenges /portal/devices has issued for a key proof, an App Attest statement or a WebAuthn link, and the freshness nonces EST /nonce has issued for a TPM key attestation, each bound to the session (or EST cookie) it was issued to and answered once.
caches.store.devices.challenges.bound: Enforced: devices.maxChallenges per realm, the oldest dropped at the insert; one per session and purpose.
caches.store.devices.challenges.hitMeani: a challenge this realm issued, so the proof was checked
caches.store.devices.events.title: Device register events
caches.store.devices.events.description: One row per device created, removed or evicted at a person's bound in this realm — what Monitoring → Devices draws over time. Never a key, a secret or an owner's name.
caches.store.devices.events.bound: Enforced: devices.eventsKept per realm, the oldest event dropped at the insert.
caches.store.devices.events.lifetime: Until devices.eventsKept newer events push it out.
caches.store.dpop.nonces.title: DPoP nonces
caches.store.dpop.nonces.description: Server-issued DPoP nonces (RFC 9449 section 8), so a proof carrying one can be checked against what was handed out.
caches.store.dpop.nonces.bound: Enforced: oauth2.dpopNonceCacheSize per realm; the oldest nonce is dropped, and a client presenting it is handed a fresh one.
caches.store.dpop.nonces.hitMeaning: a nonce found current, so the proof was accepted
caches.store.dpop.proof-ids.title: DPoP proof IDs
caches.store.dpop.proof-ids.description: The jti of every DPoP proof accepted, so a proof is good for one request (RFC 9449 section 11.1).
caches.store.dpop.proof-ids.bound: Enforced: oauth2.dpopReplayCacheSize live IDs per realm. A full history REFUSES the next proof (STS-OAUTH-0554) rather than forget a live one, which would reopen its replay.
caches.store.dpop.proof-ids.hitMeaning: a proof already used, so the request was refused
caches.store.federation.release-index.de: Which partner's release list applies to which application, built from ou=federations so a token issue does not walk the register. One index per realm.
caches.store.federation.release-index.bo: Structural: one index per realm, holding one entry per application with a release list.
caches.store.federation.release-index.se: federation.releaseIndexTtlMs ({{ms}} ms) after it was built, or at once when a federation relationship is written through this service.
caches.store.global.trusted-proxies.desc: global.trustedProxies, parsed into a BlockList, so a request does not re-parse the setting to decide whose forwarded address to believe.
caches.store.global.trusted-proxies.boun: Structural: one parsed copy of the setting.
caches.store.global.trusted-proxies.life: Until the text of global.trustedProxies changes.
caches.store.gnap.biscuit-revocations.de: The revocation identifiers of each revoked biscuit access token, published at /gnap/biscuit/revocations for a resource server that verifies biscuits on its own.
caches.store.gnap.biscuit-revocations.bo: Enforced: oauth2.maxRevokedJtis per realm — the revocation register's own bound, for the same promise about the same tokens. At the bound an expired row goes first; otherwise the OLDEST revocation is forgotten (STS-GNAP-0752), and that biscuit is accepted again by a resource server checking only this list until it expires.
caches.store.gnap.biscuit-revocations.li: until the revoked token's own exp.
caches.store.gnap.owner-lookups.title: Resource owners looked up
caches.store.gnap.owner-lookups.descript: The owner a resource server's gnapOwnerLookupUri named for an identifier, so a grant's request, approval page and issue ask the resource server once (#432 phase 5).
caches.store.gnap.owner-lookups.bound: Enforced: 1024 owners per realm, the oldest dropped and looked up again when next needed.
caches.store.gnap.signatures.title: GNAP signatures
caches.store.gnap.signatures.description: Each signed GNAP request accepted (HTTP message signatures and attached or detached JWS), so a captured request cannot be sent again.
caches.store.gnap.signatures.bound: Enforced: gnap.replayCacheSize live signatures per realm. A full history REFUSES the next signed request (STS-GNAP-0718) rather than forget a live one, which would reopen its replay.
caches.store.gnap.signatures.lifetime: Twice gnap.signatureMaxAgeS after it was seen.
caches.store.gnap.signatures.hitMeaning: a signature already seen, so the request was refused
caches.store.jose.kid-thumbprint-uris.de: The JWK Thumbprint URI published as a kid under keys.kidFormat=jwk-thumbprint-uri, keyed by the internal kid, so a token signature does not re-read the key out of its certificate.
caches.store.jose.kid-thumbprint-uris.bo: Enforced: 512 key IDs, the oldest dropped and derived again when next asked for.
caches.store.jose.kid-thumbprint-uris.li: No expiry: an internal kid is derived from the key, so its answer never changes. The oldest goes first when full.
caches.store.jose.x5c-chain-under-root.t: Certificate chains ending under the Root
caches.store.jose.x5c-chain-under-root.d: Whether a register row's stored chain ends under the current service Root, which decides whether the Root is appended to an x5c header. Keyed by the row's thumbprint and the Root's.
caches.store.jose.x5c-chain-under-root.b: Enforced: 512 answers, the oldest dropped and worked out again when next asked for.
caches.store.jose.x5c-chain-under-root.l: No expiry: keyed by the certificate thumbprint and the kid, whose answer never changes. The oldest goes first when full.
caches.store.jose.x5c-key-match.title: Certificate-to-signing-key matches
caches.store.jose.x5c-key-match.descript: Whether a certificate register row holds the signing key, asked before an x5c or x5t#S256 header is put on a token. Keyed by the row's thumbprint and the key's kid.
caches.store.jose.x5c-key-match.bound: Enforced: 512 answers, the oldest dropped and worked out again when next asked for.
caches.store.jose.x5c-key-match.lifetime: No expiry: keyed by the certificate thumbprint and the kid, whose answer never changes. The oldest goes first when full.
caches.store.keys.ca-hierarchies.title: Certificate authorities
caches.store.keys.ca-hierarchies.descrip: Each scope's certificate authority hierarchy — the service Root, a realm's Intermediate and its Issuing CAs — held decrypted for signing, read from the store at start or adopted from another process.
caches.store.keys.ca-hierarchies.bound: Structural: one hierarchy per scope (the service Root, the process branch, and one per realm), replaced rather than added to.
caches.store.keys.ca-hierarchies.lifetim: No expiry: replaced when the hierarchy changes here or on another node, and dropped with its realm.
caches.store.keys.derived-digest-keys.de: The HMAC key each keyed-digest label is derived with, so a digest does not run HKDF on every call. Kept beside the key it was derived from, which is compared on every use.
caches.store.keys.derived-digest-keys.bo: Enforced: MAX_DERIVED_DIGEST_KEYS (64) labels; past it every derived key is dropped.
caches.store.keys.derived-digest-keys.li: Until the key it was derived from changes (a new digest key or key-encryption key), which is checked on every use.
caches.store.keys.plaintext.title: Decrypted signing keys
caches.store.keys.plaintext.description: A realm's signing-key material, decrypted from the persistence store under the key-encryption key and held for an idle window so steady signing does not pay a decrypt each time. Product mode only; development keys are never stored encrypted.
caches.store.keys.plaintext.bound: Structural: one realm's key material per realm, whatever the retention policy; the policy decides only how long it is held.
caches.store.keys.post-quantum-sets.desc: Each realm's ML-DSA and SLH-DSA keys, generated (or read from the stored set) the first time something needs them, and held with the realm's key set after that.
caches.store.keys.post-quantum-sets.boun: Structural: one post-quantum set per realm, held with the realm's key set.
caches.store.keys.post-quantum-sets.life: As for the realm's key set: no expiry, dropped when the realm is removed or its keys are replaced.
caches.store.keys.signing-sets.title: Signing key sets
caches.store.keys.signing-sets.descripti: Each trust realm's signing keys (RSA, EC, and the post-quantum set once asked for), built or read from the key store on first use and held for every signature after it.
caches.store.keys.signing-sets.bound: Structural: one key set per realm, dropped with the realm or replaced when its keys are rotated or adopted.
caches.store.keys.signing-sets.lifetime: No expiry: dropped when the realm is removed, its keys are rotated, or another process's stored keys are adopted. One entry per realm that has signed.
caches.store.krb5.authenticator-replay.d: Each authenticator the protected service accepted, so a captured AP-REQ cannot be presented twice. Per trust realm: the realm whose Kerberos realm issued the ticket.
caches.store.krb5.authenticator-replay.b: Enforced: krb5.replayCacheMaxEntries per realm. A full cache REFUSES the next authenticator rather than forget a live one, which would reopen its replay.
caches.store.krb5.authenticator-replay.h: an authenticator already seen, so the request was refused
caches.store.krb5.long-term-keys.title: Kerberos long-term keys
caches.store.krb5.long-term-keys.descrip: Each registered principal's long-term keys, derived from its password with string-to-key (or read from the key source) once per encryption type and held for every ticket after it.
caches.store.krb5.long-term-keys.bound: Enforced: at most 4096 principals hold keys at once, one row per encryption type; the least recently used has its keys cleared, and derives or reads them again at its next ticket.
caches.store.krb5.long-term-keys.lifetim: No expiry: dropped with the principal, when its record is replaced (a password change or a restore), or when it is the least recently used past the bound; never persisted.
caches.store.krb5.trust-keys.title: Kerberos inter-realm trust keys
caches.store.krb5.trust-keys.description: The inter-realm krbtgt principals built from this realm's trust records (ou=kerberosTrusts), each with the keys derived from its shared password or opened from its seal, held for every referral after the first.
caches.store.krb5.trust-keys.bound: Enforced: at most 512 per realm (two keys for each of at most 256 records); the oldest is dropped and built again at its next use.
caches.store.krb5.trust-keys.lifetime: No expiry: replaced the moment its record changes (the record's bytes are compared at every use), and dropped with the record; never persisted.
caches.store.ldap.credential-tallies.des: How many people the realm defines, how many hold a password, everybody holding a credential attribute (raw), and how many of the names seen signing in are people here: the tiles of /admin/users over the whole directory without listing it (#610).
caches.store.ldap.credential-tallies.bou: Structural: one tally and one name count per realm; the tally holds the people holding a credential, not everybody.
caches.store.ldap.credential-tallies.lif: Until anything under the realm's ou=users is written, and in a process holding the directory as a window onto the store for at most ten seconds.
caches.store.ldap.device-index.title: Directory device index
caches.store.ldap.device-index.descripti: Each device entry's id, key thumbprints and Native SSO secret hash, to its entry under ou=devices, so recognising a device at the token endpoint does not copy the register (#164).
caches.store.ldap.device-index.lifetime: Until something is written under ou=devices and a lookup misses; a hit on a current entry does not wait for a rebuild. One index per realm.
caches.store.ldap.entryuuid-index.title: Directory entryUUID index
caches.store.ldap.entryuuid-index.descri: Each entry's entryUUID (and its aliases) to its DN, which is how a subject identifier and a SCIM id find a person.
caches.store.ldap.entryuuid-index.lifeti: Until the directory changes and a lookup misses; a hit on a current entry does not wait for a rebuild. One index per realm.
caches.store.ldap.group-index.title: Directory group index
caches.store.ldap.group-index.descriptio: Group membership by member and by group DN, so the groups claim and every role check do not walk ou=groups.
caches.store.ldap.group-index.lifetime: Until the directory is written in a way the index cannot fold in; the next lookup then rebuilds it. One index per realm.
caches.store.ldap.memberof-claims.title: memberOf claims, by group
caches.store.ldap.memberof-claims.descri: For each group, the entries whose own memberOf names it, so the groups and roster pages do not walk the realm once per group (#352).
caches.store.ldap.memberof-claims.bound: Structural: one index per realm, one row per memberOf value.
caches.store.ldap.memberof-claims.lifeti: Until the directory is next written, anywhere.
caches.store.ldap.person-keys.title: People, as sorted keys
caches.store.ldap.person-keys.descriptio: Every person's normalised DN and username, in the order allPersons() lists them, so a page of people does not walk, normalise and sort the realm per request (#352).
caches.store.ldap.person-keys.bound: Structural: one list per realm, the size of ou=users.
caches.store.ldap.person-keys.lifetime: Until anything under the realm's ou=users is written.
caches.store.ldap.service-accounts.title: Directory service accounts
caches.store.ldap.service-accounts.descr: The names of a realm's service accounts, so a scope decision that asks whether a person owns one does not ask the directory for all of them.
caches.store.ldap.service-accounts.bound: Structural: one list per realm, the size of its service accounts.
caches.store.ldap.service-accounts.lifet: Until a write touches an entry that is, or was, a service account; the next read then asks the directory again.
caches.store.ldap.subtree-listings.title: Directory container listings
caches.store.ldap.subtree-listings.descr: The entries under a container (applications, federations, policies and the like), kept until something is written under it.
caches.store.ldap.subtree-listings.bound: Enforced: 64 container listings per realm, the oldest dropped and walked again when next asked for.
caches.store.ldap.subtree-listings.lifet: Until an entry under the container is added, removed or written without naming where; one entry per container listed.
caches.store.ldap.username-index.title: Directory username index
caches.store.ldap.username-index.descrip: Every name a person answers to (uid and RDN), to their entry under ou=users, so a sign-in does not walk the directory.
caches.store.ldap.username-index.lifetim: Until the directory is written in a way the index cannot fold in; the next lookup then rebuilds it. One index per realm.
caches.store.mail.outbox.title: Mail outbox
caches.store.mail.outbox.description: One row per message this service sends: its recipient, its state, its attempts, when it is next due — and its body while it is pending, dead or captured, never once it is sent. The durable queue the mail.deliver job sweeps.
caches.store.mail.outbox.bound: Enforced: mail.maxRows per realm, the oldest FINISHED message dropped first; a pending one is never dropped to make room.
caches.store.mail.outbox.lifetime: Until mail.retentionS after it was queued, the oldest finished first past mail.maxRows per realm.
caches.store.mail.outbox.hitMeaning: a message suppressed as a duplicate of one already queued for the same act in mail.dedupWindowS
Each live access token's index in this realm's access-token status list — OAuth RFC 9068 tokens and GNAP's two JWT formats — with its jti, so the bit can be computed from the revocation register.
Enforced: the list holds 1048576 indexes per realm; a list with no free index REFUSES to mint the access token (STS-OAUTH-0817) rather than reuse a live one.
as long as the access token it describes; its index is free again after that.
a token's status was found here
caches.store.oauth2.access-token-status-: The last access-token Status List Token this process signed for each realm, reused while the list has not changed.
Enforced: 1024 signed lists for the process, the oldest dropped and signed again when next asked for.
until the list changes, or half of oauth2.accessTokenStatusListTtlS.
a list was served without signing it again
caches.store.oauth2.attestation-challeng: Challenges handed out for OAuth 2.0 Attestation-Based Client Authentication (draft-ietf-oauth-attestation-based-client-auth-11 section 6), so a Client Attestation PoP carrying one can be checked against what was issued.
Enforced: oauth2.clientAttestationChallengeCacheSize per realm; the oldest challenge is dropped, and a client presenting it is handed a fresh one with use_attestation_challenge.
a challenge found current, so the PoP was accepted
oauth2.clientAttestationChallengeTtlS ({{seconds}} s) after it was issued.
caches.store.oauth2.authorization-detail: RFC 9396 type definitions declared on resource applications, parsed and their JSON Schemas compiled once per distinct definition text. Shared by every realm, because the text is the key.
Enforced: 512 parsed definitions, the oldest dropped and parsed again when next used.
No expiry: keyed by the definition text, so an edited definition is a new entry. The oldest goes first when full.
caches.store.oauth2.backchannelDeliverie: One row per relying party told that a session ended (OpenID Connect Back-Channel Logout 1.0): its state, its attempts, when it is next due and the signed Logout Token. The durable queue every process sweeps; a dead letter stays until retried or retention removes it.
Enforced: oauth2.backchannelLogoutMaxRows per realm, the oldest FINISHED delivery dropped first; a pending one is never dropped to make room.
Until oauth2.backchannelLogoutRetentionS after it was queued (finished or not), the oldest finished first past oauth2.backchannelLogoutMaxRows per realm.
a delivery already queued for that session and client, so a second process ending the same session queued nothing
caches.store.oauth2.client-jwks.title: Fetched client key sets
caches.store.oauth2.client-jwks.descript: The JSON Web Key Set a client's registered jwks_uri answered with, so its client assertions, request objects and encrypted responses find its keys without a fetch per request (#120).
caches.store.oauth2.client-jwks.bound: Enforced: 256 key sets per realm, the oldest dropped and fetched again when next needed.
caches.store.oauth2.declared-authorizati: The RFC 9396 types a realm's applications declare, each with the resource that answers for it, so an authorization does not build a view of every application to find them.
Structural: one answer per realm, the size of the types its applications declare.
Until anything under the realm's ou=applications changes; the next read then builds it again.
caches.store.oauth2.redeemed-codes.title: Redeemed authorization codes
caches.store.oauth2.redeemed-codes.descr: Each authorization code already exchanged at the token endpoint, so a second exchange is recognised as a replay (RFC 9700 section 4.5, RFC 6749 section 4.1.2).
caches.store.oauth2.redeemed-codes.bound: Enforced: oauth2.redeemedCodeCacheSize per realm; the oldest redemption is forgotten. The code itself went at redemption, so a repeat of a forgotten one is still refused, as an unknown code.
caches.store.oauth2.redeemed-codes.lifet: One code lifetime after the code would have expired.
caches.store.oauth2.redeemed-codes.hitMe: a code already redeemed, presented again
caches.store.oauth2.request-uri.title: Fetched request objects
caches.store.oauth2.request-uri.descript: The content of a registered RFC 9101 request_uri, kept so a client that sends the same URI again is not fetched again (OpenID Connect Core section 6.2). Off unless oauth2.requestUriCacheS is set.
caches.store.oauth2.request-uri.bound: Enforced: 256 fetched request objects per realm, the oldest dropped and fetched again when next used.
caches.store.oauth2.request-uri.sentence: oauth2.requestUriCacheS ({{seconds}} s) after the fetch, per realm; the oldest goes first when full.
Off: oauth2.requestUriCacheS is 0, so nothing is kept.
caches.store.oauth2.signed-metadata.desc: RFC 8414 signed_metadata JWTs, reused while the metadata and signing settings they were built from are unchanged, so a busy discovery endpoint does not sign on every fetch.
caches.store.oauth2.signed-metadata.boun: Enforced: oauth2.maxSignedMetadataEntries per realm, the oldest dropped and signed again when next asked for.
caches.store.oauth2.used-assertions.desc: Every RFC 7523 JWT and RFC 7522 SAML assertion accepted, for a grant or for client authentication, so each is accepted once ever.
caches.store.oauth2.used-assertions.boun: Enforced: oauth2.assertionReplayCacheSize per realm. A full history REFUSES the next assertion rather than forget a live one, which would reopen its replay.
caches.store.oauth2.used-assertions.life: Until the assertion itself expires. Refuses new assertions when full rather than forgetting one. On a database store the rows are in the database and none is listed here.
caches.store.oauth2.used-assertions.hitM: an assertion already used, so the request was refused
caches.store.oid4vci.nonces.title: OID4VCI nonces
caches.store.oid4vci.nonces.description: The c_nonce values handed to wallets, so a credential request's proof names one this issuer issued, and uses it once.
caches.store.oid4vci.nonces.bound: Enforced: oid4vci.cNonceCacheSize per realm; the oldest nonce is dropped, and a proof quoting it is answered invalid_nonce.
caches.store.oid4vci.nonces.lifetime: oid4vci.cNonceTtlS after it was issued, or when it is used.
caches.store.oid4vci.nonces.hitMeaning: a nonce this issuer handed out, so the proof was checked
caches.store.oid4vci.status-entries.desc: Each issued credential's index in this realm's status lists and the status an administrator or a sign-out set for it.
caches.store.oid4vci.status-entries.boun: Enforced: the status list holds 131072 indexes per realm; a list with no free index REFUSES to issue the credential (STS-VC-0075) rather than reuse a live one.
caches.store.oid4vci.status-entries.life: as long as the credential it describes; its index is free again after that.
caches.store.oid4vci.status-entries.hitM: a credential's status was found here
The last Status List Token and Bitstring Status List credential this process signed for each realm, reused while the list has not changed.
Enforced: 1024 signed documents for the process, the oldest dropped and signed again when next asked for.
until the list changes, or half of oid4vci.statusListTtlS.
a list was served without signing it again
caches.store.oid4vp.sign-in-register.des: The credentials this realm issued for a person on an access token it verified, which are the only ones a wallet may sign in with — keyed by a digest of the issuer-signed JWT, or for ldp_vc by the holder key and the person.
caches.store.oid4vp.sign-in-register.bou: Enforced: oid4vp.signInRegisterMaxEntries per realm; the row issued first is dropped. That fails CLOSED — a credential with no row signs nobody in.
caches.store.oid4vp.sign-in-register.lif: until the last credential on the row expires; a disowned row is kept until then too, so that it goes on refusing.
caches.store.oid4vp.sign-in-register.hit: a presented credential this realm recorded as one that may sign its person in
caches.store.oid4vp.status-lists-fetched: Status List Tokens and Bitstring Status List credentials a trusted foreign issuer published, fetched when one of its credentials was presented to the Verifier.
Enforced: 256 fetched lists for the process, the oldest dropped and fetched again when next needed.
the list's own ttl (and never past its exp), at most oid4vp.statusListMaxCacheS; a failed fetch 30 seconds.
a presented credential's status was answered without a fetch
caches.store.oid4vp.transactions.title: OpenID4VP transactions
caches.store.oid4vp.transactions.descrip: Every presentation request this Verifier is waiting on — the bar door's and a wallet sign-in's, the latter carrying the Digital Credentials API request, its response mode and the key its answer is encrypted to.
caches.store.oid4vp.transactions.bound: Enforced: oid4vp.maxTransactions per realm; the oldest waiting request is dropped (federation.maxContexts's rule), because refusing would let anybody stop the request endpoint for everybody.
caches.store.oid4vp.transactions.lifetim: oid4vp.presentationRequestTtlS, or oid4vp.signInTtlS for a sign-in; swept when the next request is built.
caches.store.oid4vp.transactions.hitMean: a wallet's answer found the request it was made for
caches.store.oidfed.collections.title: OpenID Federation collections, made in process
caches.store.oidfed.collections.descript: The Entity Collection as this process makes it without fetching anything — this service's own realms, and subordinates already resolved — used where no crawl has been kept, so anonymous requests do not sign statements for every realm each (#136).
caches.store.oidfed.collections.bound: Enforced: 8 per realm (one per host the realm is reached by), the oldest evicted first.
caches.store.oidfed.resolutions.title: OpenID Federation resolutions
caches.store.oidfed.resolutions.descript: Trust Chains this realm resolved — by an administrator's act, or in process for its own realms — with the resolved metadata and the verified Trust Marks, so the resolve endpoint can answer without walking the federation for an unauthenticated caller (18.1).
caches.store.oidfed.resolutions.bound: Enforced: oidfed.resolveCacheMax per realm, the oldest evicted first.
caches.store.oidfed.resolutions.lifetime: Until the chain expires (its least exp, 10.4), and at most oidfed.resolveCacheS.
caches.store.passwords.breach-ranges.des: Pwned Passwords range answers, by the five-character SHA-1 prefix asked for (#62 P6): which password digests under it are known to be breached, and how often.
caches.store.passwords.breach-ranges.bou: Enforced: risk.breachCacheSize prefixes; full, the oldest is dropped and asked again when next needed.
caches.store.passwords.breach-ranges.hit: a prefix already asked, so no request was made
caches.store.passwords.breach-verdicts.d: Whether a password a door just screened is breached, for the synchronous password rules to read in the same request (#62 P6). Keyed by a digest of the password, never the password.
caches.store.passwords.breach-verdicts.b: Enforced: 1000 verdicts; full, the oldest is dropped.
caches.store.passwords.breach-verdicts.l: five minutes after the password was screened.
caches.store.passwords.breach-verdicts.h: a verdict found for a password being set
caches.store.persistence.observational-s: Whether each persisted store was declared an observation (a tally the read barrier does not wait for), read once per store handle because the check is on the path of every store write.
Structural: one flag per persisted store this build declares.
For the life of the process: a declaration cannot change while it runs.
caches.store.persistence.write-shadow.de: The last copy of each directory entry and realm record this process wrote to the persistence store, so a flush writes only what changed.
caches.store.persistence.write-shadow.bo: Structural: one row per directory entry written and one for the realm record, so at most ldap.maxEntries + 1 in a realm.
caches.store.persistence.write-shadow.li: No expiry: refreshed at each flush, one entry per directory entry and realm written. Empty in memory mode.
Certificates fetched from an Authority Information Access caIssuers URL or an LDAP cACertificate attribute, to build a path for a revocation check. Never trusted for being fetched.
Enforced: pki.revocationCrlCacheEntries, the oldest write dropped and fetched again when next needed.
caches.store.revocation.crl.title: Certificate revocation lists
caches.store.revocation.crl.description: CRLs fetched to check a presented certificate, parsed and verified, keyed by distribution point URL and the fingerprints of the signers they were verified against.
caches.store.revocation.crl.bound: Enforced: pki.revocationCrlCacheEntries, the oldest write dropped and fetched again when next needed.
caches.store.revocation.failures.title: Failed revocation fetches
caches.store.revocation.failures.descrip: A negative cache: a CRL, OCSP or certificate fetch that failed is not tried again until its retry window has passed, and the remembered failure is the answer meanwhile. A hit is a failure reused.
caches.store.revocation.failures.bound: Enforced: pki.revocationCrlCacheEntries, the oldest dropped; a dropped failure only means the address may be asked again sooner.
caches.store.revocation.ocsp.title: OCSP responses
caches.store.revocation.ocsp.description: OCSP answers about one certificate each, keyed by responder URL, issuer fingerprint and serial number.
caches.store.revocation.ocsp.bound: Enforced: pki.revocationCrlCacheEntries, the oldest write dropped and asked again when next needed.
caches.store.revocation.parsed-tiers.des: This service's own CA certificates, parsed once per PEM for the revocation register walk. Keyed by the PEM itself; a replaced CA has a different PEM and a fresh entry.
caches.store.revocation.parsed-tiers.bou: Enforced: 8192 parses; when full the whole memo is emptied and rebuilt as it is used.
caches.store.revocation.parsed-tiers.lif: No expiry: keyed by content. When full the whole memo is emptied at once.
caches.store.revocation.pem-files.title: Trust files read from disk
caches.store.revocation.pem-files.descri: The PEM files named by revocation settings, read once and kept until the file's modification time changes.
caches.store.revocation.pem-files.bound: Structural: one entry per setting that names a file (pki.revocationCrlIssuersFile, pki.revocationLdapCaFile).
caches.store.revocation.pem-files.lifeti: Until the named file changes on disk, or the setting names another file. One entry per setting.
caches.store.revocation.presented-chains: Client certificate chains, for resumed sessions

The path a verified client certificate built on a full TLS handshake, keyed by the leaf, handed back when that session is RESUMED — node gives a resumed session the leaf alone, and without this the revocation walk refuses a certificate that verified.
Enforced: 1024 leaves; the oldest is forgotten first.
Shared by every node and replicated (#406): an hour, or the main port's session lifetime and a minute when longer, renewed by the leaf's next full handshake; the oldest dropped when full.
caches.store.risk.dataset-lookups.title: Risk dataset lookups
caches.store.risk.dataset-lookups.descri: What the active geolocation, ASN and IP-list datasets said about an address, per realm. Cleared whenever a dataset version is activated on any node.
caches.store.risk.dataset-lookups.bound: Enforced: 10000 lookups, the oldest dropped first.
caches.store.risk.dataset-lookups.lifeti: Until a dataset version is activated, or the bound drops it.
caches.store.risk.standings.title: Risk standings
caches.store.risk.standings.description: Each person's last assessed risk (level, score, signals), for an issuance with no session to read it from — a Kerberos ticket, a WS-Trust token (#62 P3).
caches.store.risk.standings.bound: Enforced: risk.standingCacheSize people per process; full, the oldest is dropped, which decides that person's next sessionless issuance on roles alone.
caches.store.risk.standings.lifetime: risk.standingValidMinutes after the assessment it records.
caches.store.risk.standings.hitMeaning: a standing held and still valid, so the issuance was decided with it
caches.store.saml11.artifacts.title: SAML 1.1 artifacts
caches.store.saml11.artifacts.descriptio: The assertions SAML 1.1 artifacts stand for, until each is resolved once at the SAML responder. Keyed by the SHA-256 of the artifact, never by the artifact.
caches.store.saml11.artifacts.bound: Enforced: saml11.maxArtifacts per realm. Expired artifacts are cleared at the bound; a store still full REFUSES the next artifact rather than forget an unresolved one.
caches.store.saml11.artifacts.lifetime: Until resolved once, or until saml11.artifactTtlS passes.
caches.store.saml11.assertions.title: SAML 1.1 assertions
caches.store.saml11.assertions.descripti: Issued SAML 1.1 assertions, kept so an attribute authority request naming one by AssertionIDReference can be answered.
caches.store.saml11.assertions.bound: Enforced: saml11.assertionCacheMax per realm, the oldest dropped; an artifact naming a dropped assertion is answered as unknown.
caches.store.saml11.assertions.lifetime: Until the assertion's NotOnOrAfter, or saml11.assertionCacheTtlS when it carries none; the oldest is dropped past saml11.assertionCacheMax.
caches.store.saml2.artifacts.title: SAML 2.0 artifacts
caches.store.saml2.artifacts.description: The messages SAML 2.0 artifacts stand for, until each is resolved once at the Artifact Resolution Service. Keyed by the SHA-256 of the artifact, never by the artifact.
caches.store.saml2.artifacts.bound: Enforced: saml2.maxArtifacts per realm. Expired artifacts are cleared at the bound; a store still full REFUSES the next artifact rather than forget an unresolved one.
caches.store.saml2.artifacts.lifetime: Until resolved once, or until saml2.artifactTtlS passes.
caches.store.scim.digest-nonce-counts.de: The nonce-count (nc) values already accepted under each Digest nonce, so one response cannot be sent twice.
caches.store.scim.digest-nonce-counts.bo: Enforced: scim.maxDigestNonces nonces per realm, the oldest dropped (the nonce is then stale, and the client is handed a new one); and 1024 counts per nonce, after which the nonce is retired the same way.
caches.store.scim.digest-nonce-counts.li: Forgotten with its nonce. Persisted, so a restarted process still refuses a count it accepted; the claim a spend makes is what decides a replay across live nodes.
caches.store.scim.digest-nonce-counts.hi: a nonce count already used, so the request was refused
caches.store.scim.digest-nonces.title: SCIM Digest nonces
caches.store.scim.digest-nonces.descript: The HTTP Digest challenges /scim/v2 has handed out (RFC 7616), so a response names one this service issued.
caches.store.scim.digest-nonces.bound: Enforced: scim.maxDigestNonces per realm, the oldest dropped; a client using it is answered stale=true with a fresh one.
caches.store.scim.digest-nonces.hitMeani: a nonce this service issued, so the response was checked
caches.store.scim.hoba-challenges.title: SCIM HOBA challenges
caches.store.scim.hoba-challenges.descri: The HOBA challenges /scim/v2 has handed out (RFC 7486), so a signature names one this service issued.
caches.store.scim.hoba-challenges.bound: Enforced: scim.maxHobaChallenges per realm, the oldest dropped; a client using it is sent a fresh challenge.
caches.store.scim.hoba-challenges.hitMea: a challenge this service issued, so the signature was checked
caches.store.scim.hoba-signatures.title: SCIM HOBA signatures
caches.store.scim.hoba-signatures.descri: Each (kid, challenge, nonce) a HOBA signature arrived with, so a copied credential is refused.
caches.store.scim.hoba-signatures.bound: Enforced: scim.maxHobaSeen per realm, the oldest dropped with the challenge it was made for, so it cannot be replayed against a live one.
caches.store.scim.hoba-signatures.lifeti: Until its challenge expires; past the limit, the oldest go with their challenge.
caches.store.scim.hoba-signatures.hitMea: a signature already seen, so the request was refused
caches.store.spiffe.x509-authorities.des: Each realm's stored X.509 authorities, turned from their stored form into certificates once, for every SVID signed and every bundle served.
caches.store.spiffe.x509-authorities.bou: Structural: one unpacked authority list per realm, replaced when the stored list changes.
caches.store.spiffe.x509-authorities.lif: Until the realm's authorities are rotated or restored, which replaces the stored list the entry was unpacked from.
caches.store.ssf.dead-letter-counts.desc: An estimate of each stream's dead letters, kept so a new one can be checked against the per-stream cap without counting the queue. Letters another process wrote are not in it until the next sweep.
caches.store.ssf.dead-letter-counts.boun: Structural: one count per stream, and a realm holds at most ssf.maxStreams streams.
caches.store.ssf.dead-letter-counts.life: No expiry: recounted at each dead-letter sweep, one entry per stream.
caches.store.tls.client-certificate-iden: What a verified TLS client certificate was mapped to — a person or application in a realm, or a refusal — keyed by the leaf's digest and the authorities held when it was walked.
Enforced: 256 answers; when full the whole memo is emptied and rebuilt as it is used.
No expiry: a replaced Issuing CA changes the key. When full the whole memo is emptied at once.
caches.store.vc-api.issued.title: VC-API credentials with a status
caches.store.vc-api.issued.description: Each credential the W3C VC API issued with a status entry, and the status-list index it took, so that a status change can find it.
caches.store.vc-api.issued.bound: Enforced: 4096 credentials per realm, the oldest forgotten first (its status can then no longer be changed here; the list entry itself is vc_status.ts's and stays).
caches.store.vc-api.issued.lifetime: the credential's validUntil, or a year.
caches.store.vc-api.issued.hitMeaning: a status change found the credential
caches.store.version.stamp.title: Version stamp
caches.store.version.stamp.description: The build record (M.N.O, the commit, the build instant) read from version.json once, which every surface that draws a version reads.
caches.store.version.stamp.lifetime: For the life of the process: the build cannot change while it runs.
caches.store.version.stamp.notCountedWhy: common/version.js also runs in the remote PEP container and may not require the registry
caches.store.workers.request-affinity.de: Which request worker a browser session, a credential or a flow is pinned to, one map per pool (protocol and surfaces), so a multi-step flow stays on the worker that holds it.
caches.store.workers.request-affinity.bo: Enforced: 5000 per pool, the oldest dropped; a dropped pin is simply routed afresh.
caches.store.workers.request-affinity.se: No expiry: forgotten when its worker exits; the oldest goes first when a pool holds {{max}}. Front process only.
caches.store.xacml.parsed-policies.title: Parsed XACML policies
caches.store.xacml.parsed-policies.descr: Policies and policy sets from ou=policies, parsed and statically validated once per document text, keyed by the SHA-256 of that text so a change through any door is a new entry.
caches.store.xacml.parsed-policies.bound: Enforced: 1024 parses, the least recently used dropped; a dropped policy is parsed again when next asked for.
caches.store.xacml.parsed-policies.lifet: No expiry: keyed by content, so an edited policy is a new entry and its old parse goes when it is the least recently used.
caches.lru.default.description: A bounded cache in least-recently-used order.
caches.lru.default.bound: Enforced: an insert past the bound evicts the least recently used unpinned entries.
caches.lru.default.hitMeaning: a read answered from the cache without going to the store
caches.lru.default.lifetime: Until evicted by the bound or dropped by its owner.
caches.notListed.0.why: stored on the application entry as received, not held in memory; refreshed from the application's page
caches.notListed.1.why: held by the remote PEP container, not by this process
caches.notListed.2.why: a local of one /admin/secrets report, so a store is logged into once per report; it is gone when the report is drawn, and nothing holds it between requests
caches.remaining.untilEvicted: until the bound drops it as the least recently used
caches.remaining.untilActivation: until a dataset version is activated
caches.remaining.untilIdle: until it goes unused for the idle timeout
